newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 16.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Friday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Government to set targets for spending cuts.
-- Two 'sokaiya' racketeers arrested in Nomura Securities Co Ltd 8604T case.
-- Toyota Motor Corp plans to introduce stock option system by year-end.
-- Securities firms stop selling foreign currencies to investors because of sharp rise in yen.
-- Tokyo city government to see revenue shortfall of 310 billion yen in fiscal 1998/99.
-- North Korea may allow Japanese wives to visit home.
-- Government plans to cut public works spending by seven percent in fiscal 1998/99.
-- Electricity rate cut proposed in government action plan for sweeping economic reform.
-- United States asks Japan to use civil airports in case of emergency.
